I dette kapitel introduceres du til nogl: In this chapter you will be introduced to some of the current digital trends and how they affect various professions and us as citizens in Danish society. Regardless of which education you go to, the digital development will have an influence on the job you will do in the future.

Formålet med anvendelsen af digitale tek: The purpose of the use of digital technologies is, among other things, to make the way we work more efficient and to make contact with the public sector faster and cheaper for society and for you. At the same time, we must be critical of digital development and assess the consequences of increased digitalisation, both as citizens and as employees.
Præsentation til kapitel 1: Den digitale: Presentation for chapter 1: The digital development
Den 1. industrielle revolution foregik o: The 1st industrial revolution took place around 1760-1840, where major changes occurred in agriculture, mass production, mining and transport due to mechanization. This led to economic growth and major changes in society.
Den 2. industrielle revolution startede: The 2nd industrial revolution started around the 20th century and was mainly driven by steel and electricity, which made it possible to systematize mass production via, for example, the invention of the assembly line.
Den accelererende teknologiske og digita: The accelerating technological and digital development is changing the way companies create value and the way the public sector solves welfare tasks. The development goes by the name "the fourth industrial revolution".
I stedet for at producere mange produkte: Instead of producing many products at a time in factories in the East, you can produce closer, i.e. where the customer is.
Store, etablerede virksomheder med store: Large, established companies with large budgets often compete by producing many units of the same product at a time (mass production). That way, they can keep costs and the price of the item down. With the new technologies, there is room to come up with new ideas and to exploit the gaps in the big companies, so that the small and smaller companies have a chance to compete with the big, well-known players on the market.
Nye teknologier overtager menneskelige o: New technologies take over human tasks, e.g. in the form of robots, and help staff to make faster and better decisions, e.g. using Big Data or analysis tools.
According to Dansk Industri, Industry 5.0 covers a kind of counter movement to the increased focus on productivity under Industry 4.0. Under Industry 5.0, there will therefore be a focus on how production and industry can create value for society and the individual.
Du kan læse mere om Industri 4.0 og Indu: You can read more about Industry 4.0 and Industry 5.0 at danskindustri.dk.
3D-print er interessant for virksomheder: 3D printing is interesting for companies, as the technology can help improve competitiveness in many ways. 3D printing therefore constitutes an essential element in the 4th industrial revolution.

The Web of Things is expected to have a major impact on our everyday life, because it is not just about computing power in our everyday things, but that they are now also connected to the Internet and can communicate with other devices. The investments in the new tracking technologies are large, but it can be difficult to get all IT systems to work together.
For nogle virksomheder handler det om at: For some companies, it's about saving money (technology instead of employee salaries), while others want to change their business. A retail chain can, for example, use the tracking technology RFID to change its classic business model, where the physical store is the primary sales channel, to an omnichannel strategy that combines physical stores with e-commerce.
Ved hjælp af de nye teknologier kan virk: With the help of the new technologies, the company can optimize its business processes and thus better withstand the competition from other companies. For example, the company can with tracking technologies:
Et godt tidspunkt at optimere sine arbej: A good time to optimize your work processes is when a company takes stock. All businesses must periodically count their inventory to check what they have in stock. This is often a difficult and time-consuming process.
Hvis man bruger en almindelige stregkode: If you use regular barcode technology, you have to scan each and every barcode, and in the worst case, type the information into a computer. It works, but scanning the goods is more time-consuming than using RFID or beacon technology to take stock.
I stregkodesystemet får varen en unik ko: In the barcode system, the item receives a unique code consisting of black lines and white spaces, which can be scanned electronically. It is a so-called line-of-sight technology, where the scanner's laser beam must have visual contact with the barcode within a limited distance.
Stregkodesystemet benytter sig af det bi: The barcode system uses the binary number system. In the binary number system, ordinary numbers are written as a combination of zeros and ones. The black lines in the barcode correspond to ones, while the white spaces correspond to zeros. A thick black line means that there are several ones in a row, and the thickness of the white space indicates the number of zeros.
Der findes mere end 200 forskellige stre: There are more than 200 different barcode systems, but the most widespread is EAN, which is used on all goods in supermarkets in Denmark and internationally. So that we humans can also read the EAN code, the EAN number (typically 13 digits) is written in ordinary numbers below the barcode.
I IT-systemet gemmes oplysninger om hver: In the IT system, information about each person and/or object is stored, and therefore not much information needs to be stored in the microchip in the RFID tag itself.
RFID-teknologien kan altså hjælpe ZARA m: RFID technology can therefore help ZARA to provide better customer service and optimize its value chain. By analyzing how customers take their clothes around the store, ZARA can also come up with more optimal store layouts.

Beacon-teknologien ligner RFID-teknologi: Beacon technology is similar to RFID technology and sends out small amounts of bits, such as an ID number, to the outside world. Beacon technology works using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE), which does not use as much power as regular Bluetooth.
De fleste beacon-løsninger består af tre: Most beacon solutions consist of three parts:
Som er et stykke hardware, der sender et: Which is a piece of hardware that sends a unique ID number. It can be set to transmit at a distance of 1-70 meters.
Som kan udføre mere eller mindre komplic: Which can perform more or less complicated tasks. For example, it can send the information from a beacon to a server, and when the app gets a response back, it can show relevant information to the user.
Når serveren modtager beacon ID-nummeret: When the server receives the beacon ID number from an app, it returns a unique action to the app. For example, all information about an item such as price, weight, size etc. is displayed.
Hvad kan man ellers bruge beacons til?: What else can beacons be used for?
Med beacon-teknologien og lækre apps kan: With beacon technology and cool apps, companies can create new business models and cool user experiences. For example, your favorite store can offer you information about its products via the app while you walk around the store. Tivoli and other amusement parks can send you information about your ticket or about the length of the queue at the attractions, so that you can continuously optimize your visit. Museums can offer an audio tour where you can hear about the artwork as soon as you approach it.
Du kan som individ også få glæde af beac: As an individual, you can also benefit from the beacon technology. With the right app, and several beacons installed in your house, you can create new user experiences at home. When you get near the television, an app can turn it on, and if you approach the fridge, the shopping list appears. And the house's LED lights can turn on in exactly the colors and with the brightness you want.
For butikkerne har teknologien en stor b: For the stores, technology is of great importance. E-commerce increases competition for both good and bad. At the same time, e-commerce can also mean less revenue for the local store when you and other customers buy goods online instead.

Du og dine klassekammerater ved selvfølg: You and your classmates know, of course, that you must take care of your personal information and that you must tread carefully in the digital world. Yet several studies show that 25% of IT security breaches are due to human error. So we all have to be better at protecting ourselves and the company's data.
Men hvordan passer man på sig selv i den: But how do you take care of yourself in the digital world? You can start by staying up-to-date on technology and threats. And then you can consciously work on your behavior online and on social media. If you also ensure that unauthorized persons cannot access your data and devices, you have come a long way.
Jo mere du ved om IT-sikkerhed, jo bedre: The more you know about IT security, the better. You need to know about threats like viruses and phishing and how to create a secure password to stay one step ahead. Both as a private person and at your workplace, you have a joint responsibility for not allowing unauthorized persons into the systems. Therefore, you must e.g. learn about online threats and how to protect yourself online in this chapter.
Pas på din elektronik og sørg for, at an: Take care of your electronics and ensure that others cannot gain physical access to your devices. Should you still have your PC or smartphone stolen, it helps if they are protected with secure passwords and biometric data.
Krypter også indholdet på dine elektroni: Also encrypt the content on your electronic devices so that others cannot read the content. Even if your PC is protected with a password, an IT criminal can take the hard drive out of your PC and, with a little technical ingenuity, read the contents anyway.
Du skal være påpasselig og bruge din sun: You have to be careful and use your common sense. Therefore, in the videos below, you can learn how to spot fake e-mails and fake text messages.

Derfor skal du lære mere om de forskelli: That's why you need to learn more about the various dangers that the web contains. You must also learn something about how to best protect yourself when surfing the Internet.
Malware er software , der er designet ti: Malware is software designed to damage your computer or steal your personal information.
Når du færdes på internettet, lurer mang: When you surf the Internet, many dangers lurk. Before you know it, your computer may be full of malware, such as a virus or Trojan horse.
Du kan beskytte dig mod disse malware ve: You can protect yourself from these malware by protecting your PC with a proper antivirus program that prevents malicious software from entering your computer and company network.
En virus er et lille softwareprogram, de: A virus is a small software program that hides in other programs or in attachments. The virus can be programmed with many purposes, for example to copy itself to other computers without the user noticing.
En virus er lavet for at ødelægge og for: A virus is made to destroy and disrupt your computer's functions. There are three main reasons for developing viruses:
IT-kriminelle bruger typisk din e-mail t: Cybercriminals typically use your email to spread a virus on other computers. But the virus can also be spread through services such as Messenger, WhattsApp, etc. Therefore, a virus can be harmful to both your computer, your friends and other contacts.
Når programmet eller styresystemet start: When the program or operating system is started by the user, the virus is activated before the real software. This is how the virus starts and spreads. Most viruses are designed to replicate themselves a certain number of times before their harmful effects become apparent.
En trojansk hest er et ondsindet softwar: A Trojan horse is malicious software disguised as a useful program, such as a fake security update.
En orm er en skadelig software, som flyt: A worm is malicious software that moves from computer to computer in a network without having to be activated like a virus.
Orme udnytter svagheder i styresystemet: Worms exploit weaknesses in the operating system or web browser in the company's network, and often carry harmful programs such as a virus or a Trojan horse. Some worms can abuse the mail program's address book and forward themselves to the contacts in the address book.
Brugeren kommer derved til at installere: The user thereby installs malicious software such as a keylogger or similar software that can send confidential information behind the company's firewall and other security measures.
En keylogger er en software, der registr: A keylogger is software that records all input from the keyboard.
Det bruges til at udspionere din pc, oft: It is used to spy on your PC, most often with the aim of stealing passwords, account numbers and other sensitive information when you shop or arrange banking transactions via the Internet.

I kapitel 4 skal du lære om:: In Chapter 4 you will learn about:
Formålet med dette kapitel er, at du får: The purpose of this chapter is for you to gain a better understanding of the considerations behind the development of digital technologies and artefacts. This is important so that in the future you can help propose improvements to the digital technology used in the profession in which you will work.
I dette kapitel skal du lære, hvordan ma: In this chapter, you will learn how to go from idea to a nearly finished prototype when developing the digital artefacts. This applies both if you come up with improvement proposals for an existing artefact, and if you invent a completely new artefact yourself within your future industry.
Højst sandsynligt har disse digitale art: Most likely, these digital artefacts have gone through a thorough design development process before reaching you as a user. The companies have typically had a version 1, 2 and 10 before they were satisfied enough with the result to send the artifact to the market.
Dette udviklingsarbejde kaldes også for: This development work is also called a design process. There are different types of design processes. Here we review two of the most common: the iterative design process and the linear design process.
En prototype er en foreløbig udgave af d: A prototype is a preliminary version of the digital artefact that is under development. A distinction is usually made between initial sketches and actual prototypes, which enable user testing.
Den iterative metode kan illustreres i f: The iterative method can be illustrated in the following development model:
Figuren viser, hvordan den iterative des: The figure shows how the iterative design process goes from the initial work of identifying a problem to the idea generation phase, on to the design of sketches and prototypes, and to subsequent testing and evaluation of the test. Then a repetition of the process starts - and it is precisely the repetition of the process that characterizes the iterative design process.
Det væsentlige i den iterative designpro: The essential thing in the iterative design process is therefore that we continuously develop and test different sketches and prototypes in order to develop the best digital artefact. In this way, the risk of developing an artifact that does not create value in the industry and that no one will buy is reduced.
At arbejde iterativt betyder altså at om: Working iteratively means turning ideas into something tangible, so that we can test the sustainability of the ideas, i.e. test whether they work in practice and whether we are on the right track.
De næste afsnit gennemgår de forskellige: The next sections review the different phases of the development process:
Designprocesser behøver ikke nødvendigvi: Design processes do not necessarily have to take place iteratively. Another method is to control the process through a series of specific phases.
En fordel ved at kende alle kravene til: An advantage of knowing all the requirements for the system is that you can make a plan for the overall development process, and thus also be able to calculate a price and enter into an agreement regarding delivery of the IT system. Conversely, the disadvantage is that the model is very static. Once the requirements are defined, it is expensive to change them. Furthermore, there is not so much user involvement in the process. In the worst case scenario, you risk spending years developing an IT system and then finding out that the system does not suit the users' needs. This has been seen many times in connection with the development of larger public IT systems.
En model hvor man blander de iterative o: A model where you mix the iterative and linear design models
I virkelighedens verden arbejder interak: In the real world, interaction designers rarely work purely iteratively or linearly when developing digital artefacts. Often works in a kind of mixture of the two methods. A recognized or often used model for this is the Double Diamond model.
Den består af fire faser som hjælper med: It consists of four phases which help to ensure that you both find the right problem and work towards a good solution. The model is divided into two diamonds, where the first is about understanding the problem and the second is about finding a solution. Along the way, you work both to open up and bring out many ideas and perspectives, and to narrow down so that you choose the most important focus.

De fleste udviklingsprocesser starter ve: Most development processes start with either users or developers of a digital artifact asking questions about its current function and properties. So in the pursuit of creating better solutions, you are typically critical of an existing solution.

Når du har valgt en konkret problemstill: Once you have chosen a concrete problem to work on, you start with idea generation.
I denne fase arbejder du systematisk med: In this phase, you work systematically to process your knowledge from the analyzes of the digital artefact. The purpose is to produce different proposed solutions to the chosen problem, so it is important to get as many ideas as possible. A widely used method of idea generation is brainstorming.
I slutningen af denne fase skal du præse: At the end of this phase, you must present some selected ideas, e.g. in the form of drawings (sketches) or prototypes.

This makes the target group easier to understand because it becomes a person with real needs, behavior and habits.
Man udvikler ofte mere end en persona (c: You often develop more than one persona (around 2-3). This is because an artefact can have several different types of users, and therefore in the development process it is important to keep an eye on the needs of the different users.
Inden du går i gang med at omsætte din i: Before you start converting your idea generation into concrete proposals for prototypes, i.e. constructing the artefact, you must have an initial overview of what the artefact must be able to do. You translate this knowledge into a requirement specification.
En kravspecifikation er en beskrivelse a: A requirements specification is a description of what the artifact must be able to do. The requirements specification must therefore contain the requirements that, for example, a company has for the digital artefact they must purchase or have developed.

But at the same time it is important that you also succeed in designing an artefact that users do not get frustrated using. It must therefore be transparent which actions make the system work, and the user interface must be easy to use. This is called usability.

Effective and reliable When using the artefact, users have a natural expectation of succeeding in an action, e.g. solving a specific task, searching for information, operating a robot, etc. This must be done in a way that is acceptable to the user. The artifact must also be reliable to use, be accessible, and at the same time contain data the user can trust.
For at opnå at vores artefakt bliver bru: In order to make our artifact user-friendly, in addition to the advice on the previous page, we can make use of a number of design principles.
Når vi læser online tekster, læser vi of: When we read online texts, we often read in a different way than when we read books. Du skal hele tiden tænke på, at webstede: You should always keep in mind that the website or app should be user-friendly so that it is easy for the reader:
Ved at gøre webstedet eller appen så enk: By making the website or app as simple as possible, the reader understands the message better and mouse clicks and scrolling are minimized. You will also be more inclined to visit a user-friendly website again.
Elementer, der er placeret tæt på hinand: Elements that are placed close to each other are perceived as cohesive, e.g. image and text.
Eksempel figur 4.3: Hvis vi ser en cirke: Example figure 4.3: If we see a circle with small holes in the circumference, we will still perceive it as a circle because our brain "closes" the shape.
Lukkethed kan også tolkes som \"indhegne: Closedness can also be interpreted as "enclosed": Elements that are enclosed have something in common. We will perceive them as belonging together, even if they are different, because they are within the same framework.
Elementer, som er forbundet med hinanden: Elements that are connected to each other are perceived as belonging, for example the ribbon at the top of the Office programs or the task bar at the bottom of your screen.
Det skal være muligt at fortryde i artef: It must be possible to undo in the artefact: the user must be able to get out of "error actions", eg "back", "cancel", "undo". This makes it safe to use the artifact.
Artefaktet skal være ens og genkendeligt: The artifact must be similar and recognizable from similar solutions: Same functions and terms must mean the same everywhere.
Følg kendte standarder fx hvordan menuer: Follow known standards, e.g. how menus and buttons work. This avoids the user having to spend time figuring out how the artifact is to be used.
Artefaktet skal forhindre fejl: Det er b: The artifact must prevent errors: It is better to avoid errors than to correct them afterwards. This can be done by the system checking the input before proceeding, or by asking the user to confirm the input/action. This gives you confidence in using the artifact.
Artefaktet skal være nemt at aflæse. Bru: The artifact must be easy to read. The user does not have to remember how elements work - they must be able to quickly decipher the options, eg menus, icons and visible instructions.
Artefaktet skal passe til alle brugere -: The artifact must be suitable for all users - both beginners and experienced. For example, you can create the possibility of shortcuts for expert users and at the same time clear simple solutions for new users.
Artefaktet skal forklare fejl klart og t: The artifact must explain errors clearly and distinctly. Error messages must be in plain language and explain the problem + solution.
Artefaktet skal kunne hjælpe brugeren. D: The artifact must be able to help the user. There must be easy access to help, e.g. FAQ or guide.
